commitResults.messageTitle: Reduce repeated code in edit and its tests
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommandTest has helpers that check a successful edit and an edit
that changes nothing, but 14 tests repeat their steps instead, most
of them only to add a note to the expected message. In EditCommand,
findSkippedContexts and applyContextChanges both work out the
person's contexts after the removals.

Let's make both test helpers take the notes the result must end with,
and use them in those tests. Let's also work out the contexts after
the removals in one place, getContextsAfterRemovals.

The expected results of the tests and the behaviour of edit are
unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: edit: Keep the find results shown after editing
commitResults.messageBody:
After find, delete and archive keep the find results on screen, but
edit shows the full list again. A user who edits several people from
one search then uses an index from the old list and may edit the
wrong person.

Let's stop edit from resetting the list, so it stays as it was, as
after delete and archive. If the edit means the person no longer
matches the search, the person leaves the list, and the result adds
a note saying so and how to see all persons again.

The UG and the DG Archive feature table describe the old behaviour,
so update them too.

commitResults.messageTitle: add: Show similar-person note with phone or email
commitResults.messageBody:
add shows a note when the new person has the same name and a shared
context as an existing person, but only if the new person has no
phone and no email. Adding the same classmate again with a new phone
number or email shows no note, so a second entry for one person can
build up unnoticed.

Let's show the note whatever the phone numbers and emails are. A
person with the same phone or email as an existing person is still
rejected as a duplicate, because that check runs first.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one helper for collapsing whitespace
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand, Context, Alias and Introducer each trim a string and
collapse repeated whitespace with their own copy of the logic.
Context, Alias and Introducer collapse only spaces, so input with a
tab is rejected as invalid.

Let's use StringUtil#collapseWhitespace in all four and remove the
copies, so one place defines how whitespace is collapsed.

As a result, a context, alias or introducer typed with a tab is now
accepted, with the tab turned into a space. Saved data is unaffected,
as a tab could never be saved before.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add a use case for editing a contact
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG has use cases for adding, finding, deleting, archiving and
unarchiving contacts, but none for editing one, though edit is one of
the most used commands.

Let's add UC10 Edit a contact after UC09, in the style of UC07. Its
extensions cover an invalid index, an archived contact, invalid
details, removing the last context, a duplicate phone or email,
skipped contexts, no change and a failed save.

Appending it as UC10 keeps the numbers and cross-references of the
existing use cases unchanged.

commitResults.messageBody: The app's other messages refer to persons, so the add usage should match them.

The UG and DG used "contact" and "person" for the same entity, while
the app's messages and code use "person". Readers could think the two
terms mean different things.

Let's replace "contact" with "person" wherever it means a saved entry,
and re-render the multi-clue search activity diagram. Keep the product
name and phrases about the product category or ways of reaching
someone, such as "contact manager" and "contact details".

commitResults.messageTitle: Log the outcome of add and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
add and edit log nothing, so the log shows the command a user typed
but not what it did. Some evidence of logging is also one of the
code-quality grading criteria.

Let's give AddCommand and EditCommand a LogsCenter logger. A routine
success is logged at FINE, so it does not show at the default level.
The infrequent outcomes a developer may want to trace are logged at
INFO: add finding a similar person, edit making no change, and edit
skipping contexts.

EditCommand works out the unmatched and skipped contexts once in
execute and passes them to both logOutcome and buildFeedback, so they
are not computed twice.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep person names out of INFO logs
commitResults.messageBody: The log file persists and may be shared in bug reports. Names stay in the FINE logs, which are not written at the default level.
Add logging to add and edit

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Clarify skipped contexts and wording in UC10
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit applies removals before additions, so a context removed and
re-added in one command is re-added, not skipped. Extension 4a says
any context the person already has is skipped.

When skipped contexts are the only requested change, the app reports
both the skipped contexts and that no changes were made, but 4a and
4b describe these results separately.

Let's word 4a in terms of the contexts left after removals, cover the
combined result in 4a, and reword 3c as suggested in review.
